property_summary: After any address becomes owner via transferOwnership and calls NETM(), that owner's balance must equal totalDistributed; the mutant never credits the owner, breaking this for every such input.

For any address that calls NETM(), the caller's token balance must equal totalDistributed (250M tokens); the mutant credits totalRemaining instead, so the fuzzer finds inputs where c.balanceOf(actor) != c.totalDistributed().
After the owner calls NETM(), the owner's balance must equal c.totalDistributed(); the mutant credits totalRemaining instead, which differs whenever totalRemaining != totalDistributed.

Token conservation: after any owner calls NETM(), the owner's credited balance plus the undistributed remainder must equal totalSupply; the mutant credits totalRemaining instead of totalDistributed, breaking this equality whenever totalRemaining != totalDistributed.

After the owner initializes balances via NETM(), the owner's token balance must equal totalSupply() - totalRemaining() (i.e. the total distributed so far); the mutant credits totalRemaining instead, so once a prior getTokens() makes totalRemaining differ from totalDistributed the equality breaks.

Only the owner may invoke NETM, so for any non-owner caller and any address key, balances remain zero afterward; the mutant inverts onlyOwner, letting a non-owner call NETM and set balances[owner] to totalDistributed, breaking the rule.
